title: Care Assistant
company: Hamberley Care Management Limited - Company - Permanent
description:
Be all you can be with Hamberley
At Hamberley, we believe that our residents deserve something 'Extra Special, Every Day' and we're recruiting for a Care Assistant to help us achieve our goals.
At Chawley Grove, our Care Assistants are called Homemakers. More than support workers, care assistants or healthcare assistants - they are carers and companions all in one. They have the time to get to know our residents and are trusted to give each person the care they need, in the way they like.
Joining us at Chawley Grove, our luxury care home that provides residential, dementia, and nursing care for older people, you'll be part of a team that is genuinely passionate about the health and well-being of our residents.
Working Pattern: 12 hour shifts and working alternate weekends on a rota basis.
We offer our colleagues
- A competitive salary and benefits package
- 28 days holiday inclusive of Bank Holidays
- Quality-linked bonus scheme - A performance bonus tied to our CQC/CI quality rating, rewarding you for helping us deliver outstanding care.
- Workplace pension for your future security
- A true team culture - A collaborative, encouraging working environment where kindness, respect, and professional pride are at the heart of everything we do
- Excellent training and career development opportunities
- Employee Assistance Programme, occupational health and wellbeing support services
- Everyday saving perks - Access to a wide range of retail discounts and savings
- Free on-site parking
- Rewarding connections - Refer a Friend bonus - earn up to £750 per successful referral because great people know great people.

Be different - be a Homemaker
Be at the heart of our award winning homemaker care mode. A Homemaker is a unique caring role for a unique person, where you can care with a difference.
- A varied role where no two days are the same. Homemakers, our name for care assistants, care for individual people in the way a family member might care for someone in their home. We don't do timetabled task-based care - we care for each individual in the way that works best for them. Whether that's administering medication, helping make someone's bed, arranging a family meal with their loved ones or taking them to the beauty salon, you'll always be doing something different. Our Homemakers focus on the tiny details that make our residents unique, and tailor care to each and every individual.
- A chance to make a real difference to our residents' lives. Often healthcare assistants, care assistants and domiciliary care assistants find they don't get to spend enough time with the people they care for to make a real difference. Not at Hamberley. As a Homemaker you have fewer people to care for, but you spend more time with them. It's a more satisfying and fulfilling role that is better for our residents. That's why the model has won awards.
- Excellent opportunities for learning and development. We will support you with all the training you need, including NVQ qualifications and further clinical training if you want to specialise in areas like dementia and nutrition.
- Supportive team environment. Being kind and supportive to each other is key to our ability to show kindness and companionship to our residents. We truly believe this across all parts of our organisation. It's just one of the reasons that, when people join us, they stay with us.

Could you be part of our team?
We provide full training and induction, so we're more interested in you as a person than your specific care experience.
You may have experience as a healthcare assistant, care assistant, carer, home care assistant or domiciliary care assistant and are looking for a different approach, a nicer work environment and a more satisfying role.
If you have no work experience in care but are interested in helping people live happy lives, we'll guide you to a fantastic care assistant career at Hamberley.
What is important is that you have passion, empathy and dedication to help our residents live their lives to the fullest. We will support you with everything else!
If this sounds like you and you're looking for a fulfilling role that makes a genuine impact in the lives of others, this rewarding career is for you.
Due to the high level of interest we anticipate for this role, we may close this advert earlier than the stated closing date to manage applications effectively. If you're interested in joining us at Hamberley, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.
About Chawley Grove,
Chawley Grove, is a luxurious care home in Oxford, part of the award-winning Hamberley Care Homes - offering luxury care homes in beautiful locations throughout the UK. Residents live in spacious, stylish ensuite rooms, and enjoy beautifully furnished shared spaces and landscaped gardens. From the deluxe picture house - where we screen classic films - to the on-site luxury spa - offering hairdressing, manicures and relaxing therapies - everything has been designed and finished with the care and attention you would expect from a 5-star hotel.
Hamberley People
We respect and value our residents and each other. At Hamberley Care Homes, we believe in the importance of what we do and why we do it. Creative and empowered, our people see every day as an opportunity for growth and development. We make ideas happen. Together we can achieve anything.
Be part of something special. Be part of Hamberley.

title: Care Assistant
description:
Care Assistant

Location: Oxford

Salary: £14.37 to £15.02 with NVQ2 or equivalent

Vacancy Type: Permanent

At Fairfield, care is more than a job, it s an opportunity to change lives every single day. We re proud to provide a warm, welcoming and homely environment where residents feel valued, respected and supported to live life to the full.

As a Care Assistant, you ll make a real difference, building meaningful relationships, promoting independence and bringing comfort, companionship and happiness to our residents. You ll be joining a friendly, supportive team where compassion, reliability and teamwork really matter.

At Fairfield, we believe that the right personality matters just as much as experience or qualifications. If you re caring, compassionate and enjoy making a difference to others, we d love to hear from you! Whether you re new to care or looking to develop your existing skills, we ll support you with training, help you gain a relevant qualification if you choose to do so, and give you the opportunity to grow in confidence and build a rewarding career. And you ll be in great hands! In May 2025, Fairfield was named Oxfordshire Apprenticeship Employer of the Year (under 250 employees). We were also Highly Commended in the SME Apprenticeship Employer of the Year category at the National Apprenticeship and Skills Awards for the South-East Region in October 2025.

What we offer:
- Competitive rates of pay;
- Standard Life auto-enrolment pension scheme;
- Apprenticeships, continuous learning and development, professional development and
- Study support opportunities;
- Free meals while on shift;
- Free parking while on shift subject to availability;
- Free uniforms (or £150 annual clothing allowance for Social Wellbeing and
- Maintenance);
- An employee assistance programme with a range of services including shopping discounts, financial and legal advice, counselling and a health and wellbeing smartphone app;
- Access to chaplaincy support
- A joining bonus of £250 payable on successful completion of your probationary period.

Pre-employment checks:

All successful candidates will be required to complete satisfactory pre-employment checks, including references, an enhanced DBS check, and verification of their right to work in the UK. Please note that Fairfield is unable to offer visa sponsorship.

To Apply

If you feel you are a suitable candidate and would like to work for Fairfield Residential Home, please do not hesitate to apply.

The closing date for applications is midday on Monday 16th November 2026, but early application is advised as we reserve the right to close applications and appoint before this date for the right candidate.

title: Mental Health Support Worker- Oxford
description:
Mental Health Support Worker - Oxford

Are you passionate about supporting young people and making a positive difference in their lives?

An excellent SEN school in Oxford is looking for a compassionate, enthusiastic and motivated Mental Health Support Worker to join their team. This is a fantastic opportunity for Psychology graduates, aspiring teachers, or individuals with experience supporting children and young people who are looking to build a rewarding career in education and mental health.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide 1:1 emotional and mental health support to students experiencing anxiety, low mood, stress and other emotional difficulties.
- Support small groups through wellbeing activities focused on emotional regulation, resilience, confidence and social skills.
- Build positive relationships with students, offering reassurance, encouragement and guidance.
- Work alongside teachers and pastoral staff to implement individual support plans and wellbeing strategies.

What We're Looking For
- Compassionate, patient and empathetic, with a genuine interest in supporting young people.
- Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
- Emotionally resilient, with the ability to remain calm in challenging situations.
- Proactive, enthusiastic and willing to learn.
- Previous experience in education, SEN or mental health is beneficial but not essential.

Job Details
- Job Title: Mental Health Support Worker
- Location: Oxford
- Setting: SEN School
- Start Date: ASAP
- Pay: 93- 110 per day
- Hours: Monday-Friday, 8:30am-3:30pm
- Contract: Full-time

Apply today! This is a brilliant opportunity to gain valuable experience, develop your skills and make a genuine difference to the lives of young people, helping them feel supported, confident and reach their full potential.

Salary will be determined by the successful candidate's qualifications and relevant experience, and will be in accordance with the client's pay policy.

title: Support Worker
description:
WE ARE UNABLE TO OFFER SPONSORSHIPS

Support Worker and Healthcare Assistants - Agency

We are seeking a compassionate and dedicated Support Workers AND Healthcare Assistants to join our team. The ideal candidate will provide essential support to individuals in various settings, including home care, assisted living, and nursing homes. This role is vital in enhancing the quality of life for those in need, particularly seniors and individuals with dementia or other health challenges. As a Support Worker, you will be responsible for delivering personalised care while ensuring the dignity and respect of each individual.

Duties as a Support Worker:
- Provide patient care and assistance with daily living activities, including personal hygiene and grooming.
- Offer dementia care support, ensuring a safe and comforting environment for individuals experiencing cognitive challenges.
- Assist with meal preparation, ensuring nutritional needs are met according to dietary requirements.
- Administer medication as prescribed and monitor the health status of clients, reporting any changes to relevant professionals.
- Engage in meaningful activities that promote social interaction and mental stimulation for clients.
- Maintain accurate records of care provided and any observations during shifts.
- Collaborate with healthcare professionals to develop and implement individualised care plans.
- Provide companionship and emotional support to clients, fostering a trusting relationship.

Skills as a Support Worker:
- Strong background in patient care, with experience in senior care or hospice care preferred.
- Knowledge of dementia care principles and practices is highly advantageous.
- Ability to perform medication administration safely and effectively.
- Experience in home care settings or nursing homes is beneficial.
- Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written, with the ability to engage effectively with clients and their families.
- Empathy, patience, and a genuine desire to help others are essential qualities for this role.
- Strong organisational skills to manage multiple tasks efficiently while maintaining attention to detail.

If you are passionate about making a difference in the lives of others and possess the necessary skills to provide high-quality support, we encourage you to apply for this rewarding position as a Support Worker.

Job Types: Full-time, Part-time

Benefits:
- Referral programme

Physical Setting:
- Care home
- Nursing home
- Residential home
- Supported living

Work days:
- Every weekend
- Monday to Friday

Language:
- English (required)

Work Location: In person

title: Youth Support Worker - Oxford
description:
Youth Support Worker - Oxford

We have an exciting opportunity for a compassionate and dedicated Youth Support Worker to join a specialist school in Oxford supporting students aged 5 to 11 with Social, Emotional, and Mental Health (SEMH) needs, many of whom also experience behavioural challenges.

This role is vital in a nurturing and structured environment where every child benefits from a personalised Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP). You will work closely with students to support their emotional regulation, behavioural development, and academic progress, helping them build resilience and confidence to thrive both inside and beyond school.

Our school uses restorative practices to empower students in managing their emotions and behaviours, setting them on a path towards positive personal growth and success. You'll be an integral part of a team committed to creating a safe, supportive space that fosters wellbeing and learning.

What you'll bring to the role:
- A patient, kind, and empathetic approach to working with children facing SEMH and behavioural difficulties
- A positive mindset and a passion for helping young people overcome their challenges
- Willingness to learn and adapt to the individual needs of each child
- Previous experience working with children, particularly those with SEMH or behavioural needs, is desirable but not essential

Why this role is important:
You'll be supporting students who need extra emotional and behavioural support to engage successfully in their learning. Your contribution will help them achieve personalised goals and develop essential life skills that prepare them for the next stages of their education and life beyond school.

Whether you're a graduate seeking experience or someone passionate about making a difference in the community, this role offers valuable hands-on experience and professional development in a specialist SEMH setting.

Details:
- Location: Oxford
- Term-time role
- Salary: 90 - 100 per day
- Start date: ASAP
- Small class sizes with strong senior leadership support

If you're ready to make a real difference and grow your skills in a specialist SEMH environment, apply now! Interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis, so don't delay.

Salary will be determined by the successful candidate's qualifications and relevant experience, and will be in accordance with the client's pay policy.

title: Healthcare Assistant
description:
Agency Healthcare Assistant Bicester

Location: Bicester, Hertfordshire
Job Type: Agency / Temporary
Pay Rate: £14.80 per hour PAYE
Shift Pattern: Flexible agency shifts

We are currently recruiting Healthcare Assistants (HCAs) to work agency shifts at a well-established care home in Bicester.

This is a fantastic opportunity for experienced Healthcare Assistants looking for flexible agency work, with regular shifts available to fit around your existing commitments.

The Role

As an Agency Healthcare Assistant, you will play an important role in supporting residents with their day-to-day care and wellbeing, while promoting dignity, independence and choice.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Providing high-quality, person-centred care to residents
- Supporting residents with personal care, washing, dressing and continence needs
- Assisting with mobility and repositioning where required
- Supporting residents with meals and hydration
- Monitoring residents' wellbeing and reporting any concerns to senior staff
- Building positive relationships with residents and their families
- Maintaining accurate care records
- Working as part of a wider nursing and care team
- Following all relevant care plans, policies and procedures

Requirements
- Previous experience working as a Healthcare Assistant, Care Assistant or Support Worker
- Experience within a care home, nursing home or similar healthcare setting is desirable
- A caring, compassionate and respectful approach
- Good communication and interpersonal skills
- Ability to work effectively as part of a team
- Reliable and flexible approach to agency work
- Right to work in the UK

What We Offer
- £14.80 per hour PAYE
- Flexible agency shifts
- Regular opportunities for ongoing work
- Weekly pay
- Support from a dedicated healthcare recruitment team
- Opportunity to gain further experience within the care sector

Interested? Apply today and a member of our healthcare recruitment team will be in touch to discuss available shifts and the registration process.
